preamble: The shift from the postalveolar fricative [ʃ] to the velar fricative [x] is a case of backing or retraction: the place of articulation moves from the postalveolar region back to the velum, usually with loss of sibilance. It recurs independently in the history of Spanish and, in Slavic, where the ruki sibilant *š was retracted to *x.

examples.note: In the 16th–17th century reorganization of the sibilants, prepalatal /ʃ/ (spelled ⟨x⟩) was retracted to velar /x/ and lost its sibilance; the spelling changed to ⟨j⟩.
The ruki sibilant *š was retracted further to velar *x in Slavic.

sources: Wikipedia (2026). Phonological history of Spanish coronal fricatives. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phonological_history_of_Spanish_coronal_fricatives
